programs.title: Agents on the Line: Governing Automation at Basel's Pharma Campus
outcomes: Explain how an agent-managed, human-governed DAO assigns tasks and routes work
Identify which decisions must stay in human hands (votes, treasury, appointments)
Practice drafting a worker proposal for the Proposal Forum
Assess evidence summaries produced by AI agents

sessions.activity: Tour the charter and contribution model; map which powers are reserved for humans and why that matters for workers
Role-play the Task Router: groups route sample tasks to working groups and flag risks of automated scheduling
Compare two Evidence Monitor summaries; practice checking claims against sources and noting gaps
Draft and debate a workplace proposal; hold a mock human final vote with agents only advising

programs.data_shared: Anonymized task-routing exercise choices and mock-vote tallies, contributed as labeled training examples for shared routing and deliberation models.
programs.consent: Adult learners sign an opt-in consent form before the session; no names, employers, or personal identifiers collected; anyone may opt out of data sharing and still participate.

programs.title: River, Molecules, and Robots: A Day at the Novartis Campus DAO
outcomes: Describe how a pharma campus by the Rhine connects research, production and river
Explain that AI agents help but people decide in a DAO
Build a simple evidence summary from provided readings
Present a mini-proposal and vote as a class

sessions.activity: Story-based intro: what is this campus, what is a charter, and what jobs do agents do versus people
Small groups read short cards about a pharma topic and build a poster-sized evidence summary
Sorting game: match sample tasks to agents or humans; discuss why some decisions stay human
Each group pitches one mini-proposal; class debates and votes by show of hands

programs.data_shared: Anonymized poster summaries and vote outcomes (no names, ages beyond grade band, or school identifiers) contributed to a shared civic-education example bank.
programs.consent: Guardian/parent consent forms required for all data sharing; only first-name-free artifacts uploaded; parents may withdraw consent at any time; no photos or personal data collected.

programs.title: Evidence to Action: NGO Program Design in an Agent-Managed DAO
outcomes: Design a program around a charter's measurable outcomes
Use agent-generated research syntheses to inform intervention logic
Structure a grant proposal that humans, not agents, enact
Track and report progress against outcomes

sessions.activity: Workshop mapping mission to measurable outcomes; teams draft an outcomes ladder for a health-access scenario
Critique an Evidence Monitor summary: identify gaps, biases, and missing local context an NGO would add
Teams draft a grant proposal with the Proposal & Grant Drafter pattern; peer review before a human mock-vote
Build a simple indicator dashboard and rehearse a progress report to stewards

programs.data_shared: Anonymized outcomes ladders, proposal drafts, and peer-review comments contributed as training examples for shared proposal-drafting and evaluation models.
programs.consent: Staff opt in via organizational agreement plus individual consent; drafts anonymized before sharing; organizations may exclude client-related material entirely.

programs.title: Mission Alignment Lab: Nonprofit Governance with Human-Reserved Powers
outcomes: Explain agent-managed, human-governed structures to a board
Map human-reserved powers onto nonprofit bylaws
Draft a decision rights charter for AI assistance
Plan a stewardship and accountability routine

sessions.activity: Board-level briefing: read the charter together and identify the six human-reserved actions
Simulation: agents draft proposals, board debates and votes; reflect on where automation must stop
Draft a decision-rights matrix for your own nonprofit: which tasks agents may route, which humans must decide
Design a quarterly progress-review ritual with indicators and steward check-ins

programs.data_shared: Anonymized decision-rights matrices and governance simulation outcomes contributed to a shared governance-pattern library for other nonprofits.
programs.consent: Organizations consent as entities; individual participants opt in separately; all artifacts stripped of organization names and beneficiary data before sharing.
